model_interpretation.claim: A 2x2 output microtile gives each thread four independent FP32 accumulators while reusing each loaded A value across two columns and each B value across two rows. Keeping a 32x32 CTA output tile and 256 threads makes this a mapping comparison with the measured four-row parent rather than a larger CTA-work comparison. The mixed mapping may reduce operand loads but its 16-column half-warp access pattern may hurt coalescing; correctness, repeated timing, and register/occupancy effects need measurement.

model_interpretation.claim: The baseline assigns one output to each thread in a 32x32 CTA, with neighboring lanes advancing across rows and therefore accessing row-major A and C with strides. This candidate keeps the same 32x32 output footprint but maps lanes across columns and assigns four rows at one column to each thread. That reuses each loaded B value across four independent FP32 accumulators and may improve coalescing while reducing CTA threads from 1024 to 256; the additional per-thread state may affect occupancy. The baseline is the measured one-output-per-thread control; candidate performance remains unmeasured.

model_interpretation.claim: The measured parent uses four row accumulators per thread in a 32x32 output tile; it was correct and measured at 0.0147256 s, while the one-output-per-thread baseline measured 0.273484 s. This candidate keeps four FP32 accumulators per thread, 256 threads and 1024 outputs per CTA, but changes to one row and four column stripes per thread in an 8x128 tile. Each warp then accesses contiguous B and C stripes and reuses an A value across four outputs. This tests the opposite operand-reuse/layout mapping; its register, occupancy, correctness and timing effects remain to be measured.
